A.explanation: Work at constant pressure is $p$ times the increase in volume, $p(V_2 - V_1)$.

B.explanation: The factor $\frac{1}{2}$ is not used for constant-pressure expansion; it appears in elastic energy, not in $p\Delta V$.

C.explanation: Work depends on the change in volume $V_2 - V_1$, not the sum $V_2 + V_1$.

D.explanation: This combines both errors: it uses the sum of volumes and an incorrect $\frac{1}{2}$ factor.

hints: Notice the gas expands slowly at constant external pressure $p$ from volume $V_1$ to larger volume $V_2$.
Recall that pressure work is linked to the change in volume, so focus on $V_2 - V_1$ rather than $V_2 + V_1$.
Connect force on the piston $F = pA$ with distance moved to show work is $p$ multiplied by the volume increase.
walkthrough: Identify the process from the text and diagram: external pressure stays at $p$ while gas volume grows from $V_1$ to $V_2$.
State the rule for constant-pressure work: $W = p\Delta V$, where $\Delta V$ is the increase in volume.
Calculate the volume change: $\Delta V = V_2 - V_1$.
Substitute into the work equation to get $W = p(V_2 - V_1)$ with unit $\text{J}$ since $\text{Pa} \times \text{m}^3 = \text{J}$.
